title: review: fix round for T-1706: carry the test_dispatch_does_not_block fix (d7e45bb) onto task/T-1706
spec:
T-1706's gate is red only on tests/test_daemon.py Daemon.test_dispatch_does_not_block (0.97 s against a 0.5 s
bound), a test T-1706 does not touch; it fails the same on 1c72a58. The fix exists as commit d7e45bb on task/T-1710
(T-1710, the daemon's fix round for T-1707): the test waits on a threading.Event instead of a wall-clock bound.
In wt/T-1706 on task/T-1706: `git cherry-pick d7e45bb` (test-only change). If it does not apply cleanly, apply the same
test change by hand. Run PYTHONPATH=tests uv run python -m unittest tests.test_daemon.Daemon.test_dispatch_does_not_block
tests.test_ship tests.test_overhead. No other changes. Commit on task/T-1706.
acceptance: the named test, tests.test_ship and tests.test_overhead pass

result.summary: The Event-based test_dispatch_does_not_block is present in tests/test_daemon.py. It uses a threading.Event, asserts self.started == [] while the executor is blocked, and releases the event before settle_started. The other changes in the lineage (ship.py, test_ship.py, test_overhead.py) are T-1706's own work, and all of those files are in scope. I did not run the named tests. The packet's gate shows gate_reds 0. The earlier evidence that tests.test_ship hangs on a test this change doesn't touch is not re-verified here. The diff against task/T-1706 also shows daemon.py orphan-reaper changes and test_daemon.py orphan tests (T-1707/T-1710 history). They are outside this task's scope and come from the shared lineage, so I'm not counting them against it.

comments.issue: The Event-based assertions are weaker than the old timing bound. self.started == [] only proves the executor has not finished, not that tick() returned without blocking. If tick() ran the executor inline, the test would hang for up to 30s on release.wait and then still fail the assertion, so the failure signal is slow. Acceptable, but the 30s wait is long.
